text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Canary alert for release/2026-03-15 in inference-us-west-2. Abort criteria met: 5xx rate > 5% for 3m on route /v1/generate. Canary instances: c-canary-*-02. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/canary-failures. Incident page: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-0315-1
Alex M: ack. I'm on it. Which services are throwing 5xx?
Jordan K: logs show a mix of 502/503 from the model-runtime sidecar and occasional connection resets to the model host. Sample log: ```2026-03-15T18:07:12Z model-runtime error handler: upstream response 502; remote write tcp 10.10.5.12:443: connection reset by peer```
Priya S: I don't see any infra deploys in the window. No recent egress SG changes either. Could be a regression in the new runtime kernel selection path rolled in this canary.
Alex M: can we triage <50% rollback (kill canary) while we investigate? If abort criteria already met we should flip traffic.
ops-bot: Executing canary kill-switch: `ff toggle --env=prod --flag=canary-traffic-2026-03-15 --off` by Alex M. Result: success. Routing traffic back to stable model variant.
Mei L: Confirming: control-plane shows canary allocation scaled to 0, router swapped to stable pool. Watching error rate.
Jordan K: I pulled a few stacks from the failing pod. There's repeated TLS handshake failures to the model host followed by 502 bubbling up. Not seeing OOMs. Relevant snippet: ```ERROR: tls: handshake error from 10.10.5.12: remote error: unknown ca``` Might be a cert rotation mismatch with canary runtime and the embedded CA bundle.
Priya S: good catch. Cert rotation ran earlier today for internal services, but stable runtime seems to have the fallback bundle. Canary uses the new bundling logic — that lines up. Escalating to security-ops to confirm.
Alex M: customer impact estimate? how many requests hit the canary?
Mei L: Canary was ~1.1% of traffic during the window. Error spike lasted ~12m before kill-switch. Roughly 0.9% of total requests experienced elevated 5xx. No major customer-facing outages reported in support queue yet, but we have a few error-rate alerts from a small number of high-QPS customers — pinged account reps.
Jordan K: placing TODOs: collect kube events (`kubectl -n inference get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=c-canary-02`), gather container logs (last 15m), export model-host TLS logs, and save runtime config diff between stable and canary.
Priya S: I'm creating an incident in PagerDuty -> Severity: P2 (canary-impacting, not global outage). Assigning to infra-secrets and runtime teams.
Alex M: onboarding note: please capture the exact runtime kernel flags and CA bundles. If this is cert bundle mismatch we need a rollback plan for the CA roll or a compatibility shim.
ops-bot: PagerDuty incident created: PD-78912. Notifying security-ops and runtime.
Mei L: Post-mitigation checks: error rate back to baseline (~0.1%), latency normalized, model-serving CPU steady. I'll keep dashboards pinned.
Alex M: Handoff: I'm off at 00:00 UTC. Night on-call Sara N will take watch. Summary for handoff: canary aborted due to TLS handshake/cert bundle mismatch causing 502s; traffic rolled back to stable; P2 incident open; action items: correlate cert rotation timeline, collect runtime config, reproduce with a canary image locally.
Sara N: ack — thanks. I'll monitor the PD incident and follow up with security-ops tomorrow morning. Please add any logs or artifacts to the incident page.
Jordan K: adding steps for debug in the incident doc: commands, log excerpts, and the container image digest for the failing canary. Also saving kube snapshots to /incidents/PD-78912/artifacts.
Priya S: tagging ops runbook entries and flagging the CA rotation playbook for review with security-ops.
Alex M: closing the thread here — canary aborted and rolled back successfully. Assigning postmortem owner: Jordan K. Please file a blameless postmortem with timeline and remediation (either compatibility shim or staged CA rotation across runtime variants). If anything regresses ping @Sara N and reopen PD. :white_check_mark:
